nodes.name: Local DP strong observability
nodes.description: Local DP assumes adversaries can observe all local updates, which requires injecting substantial noise and degrades utility.

nodes.name: PN-DP relaxation
nodes.description: Pairwise Network DP (PN-DP) relaxes Local DP by modeling only pairwise observability between connected nodes, rather than full observability.

nodes.name: PN-DP amplification benefit
nodes.description: PN-DP's relaxed observability assumption enables privacy amplification by decentralization, improving utility in decentralized learning.

nodes.name: Existing PN-DP relies on RDP
nodes.description: Existing PN-DP analyses rely mainly on Renyi DP (PN-RDP), which often yields loose privacy bounds.

nodes.name: PN-f-DP introduction
nodes.description: The paper introduces Pairwise Network f-DP (PN-f-DP), extending PN-DP with the f-DP formalism for tighter, lossless privacy accounting via a hypothesis-testing interpretation.

nodes.name: PN-f-DP captures decentralization amplification
nodes.description: Unlike previous federated f-DP formulations, PN-f-DP captures additional privacy amplification arising from decentralization, random walks, and iterative communication.

nodes.name: SecLDP framework
nodes.description: Secret-based Local DP (SecLDP) considers user pairs that share secrets with neighbors and coordinate correlated noise injection to improve the privacy-utility trade-off under limited collusion.

nodes.name: Sec-f-LDP introduction
nodes.description: The paper introduces Secret-based f-Local DP (Sec-f-LDP), generalizing f-DP to regimes with correlated noise and shared secrets.

nodes.name: Sec-f-LDP amplification under collusion
nodes.description: Sec-f-LDP leverages shared secrets to incorporate correlated noise, achieving additional privacy amplification in structured collusion scenarios not addressed by standard Local DP.

nodes.name: Random walk first-visit mixture
nodes.description: The one-time snapshot observed by user j is a mixture distribution over first-visit times, since the model reaches j from i for the first time at a random step governed by the hitting time.

nodes.name: Joint concavity of trade-off functions
nodes.description: The paper leverages the joint concavity of trade-off functions to lower bound the privacy loss of the mixture mechanism by a convex combination of per-step trade-off functions.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1 mixture bound
nodes.description: Lemma 4.1 establishes a lower bound on the trade-off function of the single-observation mechanism as a weighted combination of per-step trade-off functions, weighted by hitting-time probabilities.

nodes.name: Hitting-time weighting refinement
nodes.description: The paper defines the mixture weights based on the hitting-time distribution rather than matrix power entries (W^t)_ij, better capturing random walk dynamics and yielding tighter bounds.

nodes.name: Recursive computation of hitting weights
nodes.description: The hitting-time weights are computed recursively via the Markov property, based on the transition matrix W.

nodes.name: Per-step trade-off via composition
nodes.description: Each per-step trade-off function is computed using the composition rule of f-DP to account for the cumulative privacy effect of local SGD updates.

nodes.name: Amplification by iteration for strongly convex losses
nodes.description: For strongly convex and smooth loss functions, privacy amplification by iteration in f-DP is applied, using the contraction effect together with repeated noise injection to yield tighter trade-off functions (Lemma 4.2).

nodes.name: Standard composition for non-convex losses
nodes.description: For general non-convex loss functions, the standard f-DP composition rule is used instead, yielding a more conservative bound (Lemma 4.3).

nodes.name: Markov chain concentration for visit counts
nodes.description: A Hoeffding-type concentration inequality for Markov chains is used to bound the total number of times node j is visited during training.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.1 user-level guarantee
nodes.description: Theorem 4.1 combines the single-visit mixture bound with the Markov concentration bound on visit counts to yield the final user-level PN-f-DP guarantee for Algorithm 1, computable numerically though lacking closed form.

nodes.name: Tighter RDP conversion from hitting times
nodes.description: Converting the f-DP guarantees back into RDP yields improved bounds compared to prior work, primarily due to the more accurate modeling of communication timing via hitting times.

nodes.name: Record-level adjacency
nodes.description: Record-level privacy considers datasets differing by a single record within one user's local dataset, rather than the entire user dataset.

nodes.name: Sub-sampling amplification
nodes.description: In the record-level setting, each user computes a gradient from a random subset of local data, reducing the probability a given record is selected and amplifying privacy via sub-sampling.

nodes.name: Sub-sampling interacts with iteration amplification
nodes.description: Sub-sampling interacts with privacy amplification by iteration, making the record-level analysis more intricate than the user-level analysis.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4 record-level trade-off
nodes.description: Lemma 4.4 characterizes the record-level trade-off function using a sub-sampling operator applied to the per-step Gaussian trade-off bounds.

nodes.name: Record-level guarantee via substitution
nodes.description: The record-level privacy guarantee is obtained by substituting the record-level trade-off function from Lemma 4.4 into Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 4.1.

nodes.name: Honest-but-curious collusion model
nodes.description: The correlated-noise analysis models honest-but-curious collusion at level q, where a coalition of up to q users may pool information including shared secrets.

nodes.name: Algorithm 2 correlated + independent noise
nodes.description: Algorithm 2 (DecoR) incorporates both independent Gaussian noise and pairwise correlated noise via shared secrets before mixing via the transition matrix.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.2 Sec-GDP guarantee
nodes.description: Theorem 4.2 shows Algorithm 2 satisfies (mu, S)-SecGDP against colluding users, with mu expressed in terms of independent noise variance, correlated noise variance, collusion level, and the graph Laplacian's second eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Tighter (eps,delta) bounds vs RDP
nodes.description: Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show f-DP-based accounting yields consistently tighter (epsilon, delta) bounds than RDP-based approaches.

nodes.name: Tighter bounds require less noise
nodes.description: Tighter (epsilon, delta) bounds allow calibrating less noise for a given privacy level.

nodes.name: Improved utility
nodes.description: Requiring less noise for the same privacy guarantee leads to significantly improved model utility.

nodes.name: Hypercube graph pairwise comparison
nodes.description: On a hypercube graph with 32 nodes, PN-f-DP yields noticeably smaller pairwise privacy budgets epsilon than PN-RDP across nearly all node pairs.

nodes.name: Refined RDP hitting-time baseline still worse
nodes.description: Even against a refined RDP baseline using exact hitting times rather than an upper bound, PN-f-DP consistently yields the smallest epsilon.

nodes.name: MNIST/logistic regression accuracy gains
nodes.description: On MNIST classification and logistic regression tasks under an expander graph topology, the f-DP-calibrated method achieves consistently higher test accuracy than RDP-based methods across graph structures and privacy budgets.

nodes.name: Sec-f-LDP improved trade-off vs SecLDP and LDP
nodes.description: On ring and torus topologies with logistic regression on the a9a dataset, Sec-f-LDP achieves a better privacy-utility trade-off than both SecLDP and local DP baselines.

isolated_nodes.name: FL motivation
isolated_nodes.description: Federated Learning enables user devices to collaboratively train models without sharing raw data, useful when a central server is unavailable, untrusted, or communication is expensive.

isolated_nodes.name: Model updates leak information
isolated_nodes.description: Even without access to raw data, model updates can reveal sensitive information, especially under inference or reconstruction attacks.

isolated_nodes.name: DP-SGD baseline mechanism
isolated_nodes.description: DP-SGD adds noise to stochastic gradients to provide a formal differential privacy guarantee.

isolated_nodes.name: Privacy accounting affects utility
isolated_nodes.description: More accurate privacy accounting allows adding less noise for the same guarantee, improving utility.

isolated_nodes.name: Trade-off function definition
isolated_nodes.description: The trade-off function T(P,Q) denotes the minimal type II error at a given level of type I error in the hypothesis-testing formulation of differential privacy.

isolated_nodes.name: Gaussian DP special case
isolated_nodes.description: A mechanism satisfies mu-Gaussian DP if its trade-off function equals that of two unit-variance Gaussians separated by mu.

isolated_nodes.name: Tensor product composition
isolated_nodes.description: The composition of DP mechanisms corresponds to the tensor product of their trade-off functions.

isolated_nodes.name: User-level vs record-level DP granularity
isolated_nodes.description: User-level DP bounds the influence of an entire user's dataset, while record-level DP limits the impact of a single data point within a user's dataset.

isolated_nodes.name: Algorithm 1 decentralized DP-SGD
isolated_nodes.description: Algorithm 1 performs K local SGD steps with Gaussian-perturbed gradients at each active node, then sends the model to a randomly chosen neighbor via a random-walk transition matrix.

isolated_nodes.name: Privacy amplification by shuffling and decentralization
isolated_nodes.description: Privacy amplification can arise from both shuffling techniques and decentralization of communication.

isolated_nodes.name: Privacy amplification by iteration
isolated_nodes.description: In iterative processes, revealing only the final model parameter (not intermediates) contributes additional privacy amplification, previously extended to f-DP via a shifted interpolated process.

isolated_nodes.name: Prior random-walk analysis limited to RDP
isolated_nodes.description: The privacy impact of random walks had previously only been studied under RDP, leaving its characterization within f-DP an open question prior to this work.

isolated_nodes.name: Communication graph and transition matrix
isolated_nodes.description: Decentralized communication is modeled via a connected graph with an associated Markov transition matrix governing message-passing probabilities between nodes.

isolated_nodes.name: Remark 3.1 weak federated f-DP relaxation
isolated_nodes.description: Record-level PN-f-DP is shown to be a relaxation of weak federated f-DP from prior work, connected via a double convex conjugate operation.

isolated_nodes.name: Spectral gap assumption in Theorem 4.1
isolated_nodes.description: Theorem 4.1 assumes the transition matrix is irreducible, aperiodic, and symmetric with a positive spectral gap, used to bound the number of node visits with high probability.

isolated_nodes.name: Framework generalizes to dynamic graphs
isolated_nodes.description: The proposed framework generalizes to dynamic or time-varying graphs by updating the transition matrices each round, and extends to other decentralized protocols such as gossip-based or push-sum algorithms.

structural_reasoning: The graph is highly coherent within its major thematic clusters: the PN-DP to PN-f-DP motivation chain (C1), the SecLDP to Sec-f-LDP motivation chain (C2), the detailed user-level privacy analysis pipeline combining random-walk mixtures, joint concavity, and Markov concentration into Theorem 4.1 (C3), the record-level extension via sub-sampling (C4), the correlated-noise Sec-GDP result (C5), and the experimental validation cluster tying tighter bounds to improved utility across three experimental settings (C6). Edges within C3 and C6 carry slightly lower edge_scores reflecting that some connections (e.g., between the RDP-conversion improvement and the final theorem, or between the SecLDP amplification claim and the experimental trade-off result) are supported by the overall narrative and figure captions rather than a single explicit causal sentence. No cycles or reversed dependencies were identified; most nodes are prerequisite building blocks feeding into their respective section's culminating theorem or empirical claim. A relatively large isolated-node set reflects background definitions (f-DP formalism, DP notions, algorithm descriptions) that motivate but are not directly chained to specific downstream results with enough evidentiary specificity.
